items.text: A page file whose name holds a malformed percent escape, or (with `:file/name-format :triple-lowbar`) an empty namespace part, now gets the page name Logseq gives it: `%E9.md` is the page `%E9` (was `�`), `___lead.md` is `lead` (was `/lead`), `a______b.md` is `a/b` (was `a//b`), and in the default Legacy format `50%25 of 100%.md` is `50%25 of 100%`. Such a page now has a new name: a link written with the old name (`[[a//b]]`) no longer reaches it, and its linked references follow the new name. `caf%C3%A9.md` stays `café` (REG-CM-NAMES-MALFORMED-ESCAPE, REG-CM-NAMES-EMPTY-NAMESPACE-PART).

regressionEvidence.reason: Existing catalog coverage: REG-CM-NAMES-MALFORMED-ESCAPE: A file name with a malformed percent escape (pages/%E9.md, bad%E9.md, or in a Legacy graph 50%25 of 100%.md) was named with a replacement character or decoded differently from OG ("�", "bad�", "50% of 100%"), so OG's links to it ([[%E9]]) opened a new empty page in Tine and two files could collapse to one name. It now gets OG's name ("%E9", "bad%E9", "50%25 of 100%"); caf%C3%A9.md stays "café"; REG-CM-NAMES-EMPTY-NAMESPACE-PART: In a triple-lowbar graph a file name with an empty namespace part (pages/___lead.md, a___.md, a______b.md) was named "/lead", "a/", "a//b"; OG names them "lead", "a", "a/b", so OG's [[a/b]] opened a new empty page in Tine instead of that file. items.text: A rename now changes exactly what Tine reads as a reference to the page, and nothing else. items.text: Typing a link, tag or alias costs work in proportion to what changed, not to the size of the graph. An autosave while typing inside `[[…]]`, `#tag` or `alias::`, or linking a page that already exists, no longer reloads the list of every page name: Tine sends only the names that appeared or disappeared, which was about 2.6 MB per save on a 10,000-page graph. `[[` suggestions no longer reread every page on each keystroke, and property-name suggestions after `::` load the property names once when the list opens and the values only for the property you pick, instead of every property and value on each keystroke. Suggestions are unchanged (REG-PERF-LINK-EDIT-INVENTORY-REFETCH, REG-PERF-COMPLETION-GRAPH-WALK).

regressionEvidence.reason: Existing catalog coverage: REG-PERF-LINK-EDIT-INVENTORY-REFETCH: Every autosave while typing inside [[...]], #tag or alias::, and linking a page that already exists, refetched the whole page inventory (about 2.6 MB and 70 ms per save on a 10k-page graph) and rebuilt the window's name maps; REG-PERF-COMPLETION-GRAPH-WALK: Each [[ completion keystroke re-read every page's referenced names, and each property-name completion keystroke fetched every property key with all its values, so completion slowed with graph size (66 ms and 128 ms per keystroke on a 10k-page graph). The referenced test files exist; their suites were not rerun for this metadata-only preparation.
